title: Spire Rewind - Checkpoints, Undo & Run Replay
description:
[b]Spire Rewind[/b] is a save checkpoint and undo mod for Slay the Spire 2. It keeps a checkpoint every time the game saves your single-player run, so you can rewind to an earlier floor from the pause menu or the main menu. Use it to retry a fight, recover from a misclick or save scum without copying files by hand. It also logs the choices of every floor and the decision points of every fight, and exports the whole run as one offline HTML replay that opens in any browser.

回溯存檔：每次遊戲存檔時自動建立檢查點，可以退回之前的樓層重打，也能把整局匯出成 HTML 回放。

[b]Minimum game version 0.107.1, tested only on v0.107.1, singleplayer only.[/b] On a newer game version the mod may or may not load; if it loads, the Rewind dialog shows a notice. A checkpoint taken on a different game version is never restored.

[h2]Read this before you rely on it[/h2]
[list]
[*]A rewind [b]rewrites the active run save[/b]. The mod saves a recovery checkpoint first and tries to put the original save back if loading fails, but it has [b]not been tested with Steam Cloud sync[/b] yet. Back up your save folder before using it on a run you care about. If a rewind fails and the dialog names a backup id, the README in the mod folder explains how to put that checkpoint back by hand with the game closed.
[*]Progress, unlocks, statistics, achievements and run history are [b]not[/b] rewound. The mod never touches those files, and a replayed fight can count again in the statistics.
[*]Checkpoints follow the game's own save points (entering and finishing a room), not every turn.
[/list]

[h2]Install[/h2]
[list]
[*]Subscribe and start the game. The first time the game finds a new mod it asks whether to load mods; allow it.
[*]Install it once only: do not also put a copy in the game's [i]mods[/i] folder. With the same mod in both places the game loads only one of them.
[*]Modded play uses a separate set of save files. Your unmodded saves and progress are not touched.
[*]To turn it off for a while, disable it in the Modding tab of the game's settings, or start the game with [i]-nomods[/i].
[*]To remove it, unsubscribe. Checkpoints and exports stay in the profile's [i]rewind[/i] folder (under [i]modded/profileN[/i] in the game's save location); delete that folder too if you want them gone.
[/list]

[h2]Use[/h2]
[list]
[*]In the pause menu, or in the main menu while a run can be continued, choose [b]Rewind[/b]. Each row is one checkpoint: act, floor, room, HP, gold, deck size and time. Pick one, read the warning, confirm.
[*][i]Entering room[/i] is the save taken before the room starts; use it to replay a fight. [i]Room completed[/i] loads with the room already finished.
[*][b]Rewind settings[/b] in the same dialog: checkpoints on or off, how many recent runs to keep, whether rewound runs are marked in the mod's own records, and the interface language (follows the game, or Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, English).
[*][b]Export this run replay[/b] writes one HTML file to the profile's [i]rewind/exports[/i] folder.
[/list]

[h2]Local data[/h2]
Checkpoints, choice logs, combat archives and exports are stored only on this computer, in the current profile's [i]rewind[/i] folder. They are not synced to Steam Cloud. The mod has no telemetry and no network service of its own. A rewind writes the run save through the game's own save system, which Steam Cloud may sync like any other save.

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
Works alongside [b]Spire Link[/b]; both were tested together on v0.107.1. No other mod is required. Daily runs, multiplayer and ended runs are not supported.

[h2]For developers[/h2]
Source code, data formats and release zips: [url=https://github.com/PingChunChung/spire-rewind]github.com/PingChunChung/spire-rewind[/url]

changeNote: 0.1.0: first release. Automatic checkpoints at the game's save points, rewind with confirmation and a recovery checkpoint, per-floor choice log, fight decision snapshots, offline HTML replay export; the Rewind dialog shows a notice on untested game versions. Tested on game v0.107.1, singleplayer only; not yet tested with Steam Cloud sync.
